doc.title: Frank Strazzeri interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Recording versus live playing
summary: He likes the quiet of the studio, but is hot and cold depending on piano and room.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Do you think you play as well on record as you do in live situations?

Well that’s hot and cold. That’s a hot and cold subject. You can be great in the studio — a lot of times it all depends on the piano you’re playing on, at least with me. It could be the piano I’m playing on, it could be the room I’m in, I like the sound of it, it could be I like the bass player or I don’t like this or I don’t like that and I think that has a lot to do with my being hot and cold. Just to get a more direct answer to what you asked me, I find I like to record. I like to record because it’s quiet and there’s no distractions, and I can concentrate. I don’t have to perform for people, you know what I mean? It’s like a boxer. When he practices in a ring and he practices and is working out, he certainly is not the same guy that when he gets in front of a huge crowd, you know, like a championship fight. Them guys, their adrenaline gets up. Sometimes when your adrenaline gets up it works against you. You get too dramatic, you get too energized. I find that kind of thing sometimes doesn’t work in my behalf. Sometimes I think conditions forcing you to lay low sometimes get me in a better groove as far as playing. Strange question, but it’s true, that does arise. It’s something to think about.
